approachQuestion.prompt:
Measure the longest numbered stretch

Input: an unsorted array codes of integers, possibly with duplicates. Return the largest number of distinct consecutive integers all present in codes. Their positions need not be adjacent. Return 0 for an empty array.

Example 1: codes = [11, 5, 9, 10, 5, 8]. Output: 4, for 8,9,10,11. Example 2: codes = [3,3,3]. Output: 1. Example 3: codes = [-2,0,-1,7]. Output: 3.

Constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200,000; −1,000,000,000 ≤ codes[i] ≤ 1,000,000,000. Neighbor arithmetic uses signed 64-bit integers. Do not mutate input. Prefer the least expected running-time growth, then avoid unnecessary asymptotic auxiliary storage. Integer hashing has expected amortized constant-cost operations under non-adversarial hashing.

options.text: Build a set of distinct codes. For each set value x, walk forward through successive values only if x−1 is absent; update the longest length.
options.feedback: Every distinct value belongs to one stretch and is visited by a forward walk from that stretch’s unique start, so walks do not repeatedly traverse the same stretch.

options.text: Comparison-sort a copy, ignore equal neighbors and count consecutive runs.
options.feedback: Sorting and ignoring duplicates gives the right length, but ordering the full array is removable when membership can be queried directly.

options.text: Build a set and launch a forward membership walk from every distinct value, taking the longest.
options.feedback: This is correct but substantially inefficient: one long stretch is walked again from each of its values, repeating most of the same work.

options.text: Scan the supplied array and extend a run only when the next array entry equals the previous entry plus one.
options.feedback: For [2,1], the answer is 2 even though the array has no increasing adjacent run of length 2. Input adjacency is irrelevant.

feedback.reason: Recognize that only the first value of a consecutive component should launch a forward walk.
details: Build a set of distinct codes. Iterate its values. A value whose predecessor is present is skipped; otherwise walk upward until the next value is absent, and update the maximum length.
Only a value with no predecessor starts a stretch. Every distinct value is then walked through in one component, so nested-looking loops do not rescan every component from every member.

“Build a set of distinct codes. For each set value x, walk forward through successive values only if x−1 is absent; update the longest length.”: Every distinct value belongs to one stretch and is visited by a forward walk from that stretch’s unique start, so walks do not repeatedly traverse the same stretch.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Walk only from stretch starts”, n is input length and u is its number of distinct codes. Choose its time and auxiliary-space pair. Use the tightest standard bound for the worst legal input of size n, with expected time over non-adversarial hashing. Fixed-width integer and fixed-size tuple hash operations take expected amortized O(1); arithmetic, comparison and copying one integer take O(1). Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input and returned result, includes all maps, sets, temporary copies and call stacks. The method is iterative, with constant call-stack space.

options.text: Expected O(n + 1) time; O(u + 1) auxiliary space.
O(n log n + 1) time; O(n + 1) space.

feedback.reason: Each distinct code participates in only one forward component walk.
details: Recognize that only the first value of a consecutive component should launch a forward walk.
Building the set processes n entries. Iteration checks u predecessors, and all forward walks together visit u distinct values plus at most u missing endpoints. Expected O(n + 1).
O(u + 1) for the set and scalar counters; no input copy or recursion.
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(u + 1) auxiliary space.”: Correct under the stated expected/amortized hashing model.
“Expected O(nu + 1) time; O(u + 1) space.”: Walks are disjoint because only stretch starts launch them; this is not the walk-from-every-value alternative.
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(1) space.”: The set stores u distinct codes.
“O(n log n + 1) time; O(n + 1) space.”: The fixed method uses membership queries and performs no sorting or input copy.
